newsitem.title: ESTONIA: INTERVIEW-TALLINNA SEES NO NEED FOR MERGER.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-TALLINNA SEES NO NEED FOR MERGER.

text.p: Estonia's Tallinna Pank said on Wednesday that it saw no need for a merger with another bank in the short term and would have a clearer strategy for the Baltic market as a whole in late 1997.

Merger talk has begun to creep into the market as leading bank Hansapank said it was prepared to link with a foreign bank to enter Lithuania while Hoiupank said it was ready to merge with a local bank.
But Tallinna Pank deputy chairman Targo Raus dismissed any talk of his bank merging for now because the growth of its market share has been relatively normal.
"No mergers are seen in the short-term," Raus told Reuters.
Tallinna Pank is the fourth largest commercial bank in Estonia with assets of 2.6 billion kroons at the end of May.
"But in theory it is easier to get clients when you buy them together with an organisation," he added.

Raus said that it was a very sensible idea for Hoiupank to consider merger in order to diversify its client base and activities. Tallinna Pank and Hoiupank have not been in concrete talks to merge, Raus added.
He also said that the bank's plans for Estonia would depend on its ideas for the rest of the Baltic market.

"We need to analyse possible acquisitions in Latvia and Lithuania...before forming new plans in the Estonian market," Raus said, adding that the picture would look clearer in the latter part of the year.
"Our strategy in Latvia and Lithuania foresees that we could acquire something but it is not decided if and when," Raus said.
Tallinna last December bought a 20-percent stake in Latvia's Saules Banka. It is also active in leasing in Latvia and Lithuania and wants to start banking in Lithuania.
